subject.title: [Feature]: Expose Discord slash interaction response controls to plugin commands

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord-specific command responder on PluginCommandContext, or design a generic channel responder capability for plugin commands?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but either path expands the public Plugin SDK and channel boundary; automation cannot choose the permanent API shape or auth/routing constraints safely.

options.title: Add a generic responder capability
options.body: Expose a narrow capability-gated responder contract that Discord can implement for defer, reply, follow-up, and edit while preserving the existing returned ReplyPayload fallback for all plugins.

options.title: Add Discord-only ctx.discord.respond
options.body: Ship the user-requested Discord-specific shape faster, accepting an owner-specific SDK surface that may need later generalization for Slack or other native command channels.

options.title: Keep the current return-payload model
options.body: Decline per-interaction response controls for plugin commands, keeping the SDK smaller but leaving mixed visibility and edit flows unsupported for Discord plugins.

recommendation.title: Add a generic responder capability
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow capability-gated responder contract that Discord can implement for defer, reply, follow-up, and edit while preserving the existing returned ReplyPayload fallback for all plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history put steipete on the current PluginCommandContext and Discord native-command implementation, and this choice is a public SDK boundary decision.
